_comment: Per-ja_id rejections that no structural filter in build-corpus.py can express — a single sentence, or a single Japanese↔French pairing, judged wrong by hand-inspection rather than by a rule. Each entry's reason is the record of that judgement. Keys are Tatoeba jpn_sentences ids (as strings, JSON has no integer-keyed maps); build-corpus.py loads and int()s them before filtering. This file is read at build time and is never edited by apply-tatoeba-sentences.py or hand-patched into sentences.json — sentences.json stays fully generated.
1889539: あなたは毎日にここへ来る？ is ungrammatical: 毎日 is a bare temporal adverb and does not take the particle に. It cleared every structural filter and was filed under 毎日 — removed by hand-inspection, not a rule (2026-08-15).
195385: また来てください。 was paired with the French «J'espère que tu vas rappeler.», which mistranslates the imperative 「来てください」 ("please come again") as a hope-clause about a phone call. Removed rather than corrected: the app promises verbatim Tatoeba French, and editing the gloss would make that promise false a second time.
83717: 分かりますか。 was paired with the French «Pouvez-vous répondre à cela ?», which answers a different question than "do you understand?". The Japanese itself is fine — only this ja_id↔fr_id pairing is blocked, so a future run with a different (correct) French translation for the same Japanese sentence could pass again.
214829: すぐに分かりますよ。 was paired with the French «Vous ne pouvez pas le rater.», which reads as an English-relay gloss ("you can't miss it") rather than a translation of 分かる ("to understand/become clear"). Same reasoning as 83717: block the pairing, not the Japanese.
222749: この花が何本かほしいのですか。 was paired with the French «Veux-tu une de ces fleurs ?» ("do you want one of these flowers"), but 何本か means "several/a few", not "one". Same reasoning as 83717/214829.
